prompt: Hall A charges $\$40$ plus $\$6$ per guest. Hall B charges $\$10$ per guest with no rental fee. Solve $40 + 6g = 10g$ to find the number of guests $g$ where the two halls cost the same. Give just the number.
hint: Guests appear on both sides of the equation. Collect the $g$ terms on one side before dividing.

hints.text: Guests appear on both sides of the equation. Collect the $g$ terms on one side before dividing.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test one guest count: at $5$ guests, Hall A costs $40 + 30 = 70$ and Hall B costs $50$. Keep testing, or set the two costs equal.
Subtract $6g$ from both sides to get $40 = 4g$. Then divide both sides by $4$.
$40 \div 4 = 10$, so the halls cost the same for $10$ guests.

explanation: Subtract $6g$ from both sides so the variable is only on the right: $40 = 4g$.
Divide both sides by $4$ to undo the multiplication, which gives $g = 10$.
Check: Hall A costs $40 + 6(10) = 100$ dollars and Hall B costs $10(10) = 100$ dollars, so they match at $10$ guests.

alternativeExplanations.title: Close the gap
steps: Hall B costs $\$4$ more per guest, but hall A starts with a $\$40$ fee.
Every guest closes the gap by $\$4$, so it takes $40 \div 4 = 10$ guests to tie.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Giving Hall B a $40 fee too — writing 40 + 6g = 40 + 10g — makes the halls tie forever.
Each hall keeps its own rule: A is 40 + 6g, B is just 10g. Set THOSE equal, and g = 10 falls out.
